subject: MAP: final token reconciliation & prefetch/batching assumptions for close timeline
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: final token reconciliation & prefetch/batching assumptions for close timeline

Sara —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our MAP, we want to lock the economic assumptions that will drive your procurement signoff. Below is a draft of the token/unit reconciliation and the prefetch/batching assumptions we plan to include in the final MAP. Can you confirm these items and the target close date (you mentioned late June)? If you prefer, we can put a summary into the SOW addendum for procurement.

Key assumptions (draft):
- Unit price: calculated as tokens per $ using a blended profile. Baseline: 1,800 tokens per $ for the chat tier (model: mix of 13B quantized + fallback 70B).
- Peak vs steady traffic: simulations assume 4x peak factor for 2% of requests; steady-state traffic used for billing runway.
- Batching: preferred setting = 50ms max latency bucket; average batch size ~6 tokens per request during steady-state (we simulated 95th p50).
- Prefetch / KV cache: we expect a 12% token reduction from prefix caching and prefetch warmup on repeat queries for the triage flows you showed.
- Fallback routing: when dedicated capacity is saturated, requests fall back to hosted with a 1.3x token cost multiplier (network/reprompt overhead).

What I need from you to finalize this in the MAP:
1) Procurement confirmation of target close date and whether Beacon will require a PO up front or on-boarding invoice.
2) Any additional traffic profiles (sample logs) that change the repeat-query rate — that materially affects the prefetch discount.
3) Approval to include our recommended batching/prefetch defaults in the SOW appendix (these are conservative; we can tighten after pilot).

I'll follow up with a narrow reconciliation spreadsheet to show tokens-per-session by workflow. Attaching a first-pass model (token_model_v2.xlsx) and a one-page MAP action list.

Best,

David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: token_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx), MAP_action_items.pdf (pdf)

From: Sara Liu <sara@beaconhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Beacon Procurement <procurement@beaconhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: final token reconciliation & prefetch/batching assumptions for close timeline

David —

Appreciate this clear summary. Quick answers:
- Target close: we are aiming for a contract signature by 2026-06-30, procurement needs the final numbers by EOD 2026-06-24 to process the PO.
- PO vs invoice: we will issue a PO; Beacon requires an initial monthly invoice tied to a pilot milestone before larger commits.
- Traffic samples: I asked our analytics team to pull two weeks of anonymized API transcripts for triage flows — will share by Monday (2026-06-15).

On the assumptions: the prefetched cache % looks reasonable based on our usage pattern but the team flagged the 12% number as optimistic until they see the sample logs. Also: can you provide the sensitivity view showing tokens/$ if prefetch only yields 6% and if batching is constrained to 2 per batch? Procurement will want the worst-case lane for unit economics.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with procurement for the PO timeline.

Sara
Sara Liu
Product Lead, Conversational Care | Beacon Health

Thanks —
David

Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: MAP: final token reconciliation & prefetch/batching assumptions for close timeline

David / Team —

Attached (prefetch-sim-results.csv) is a quick sensitivity run I did using existing telemetry from similar triage flows. Notes:
- Baseline tokens per $ (no prefetch, batch size = 2): ~950 tokens/$.
- Mid case (6% prefetch, batch size = 3): ~1,150 tokens/$.
- Best case (12% prefetch, batch size = 6): ~1,760 tokens/$.
- Fallback hosted multiplier: we should model 1.25x for cold-network fallbacks and 1.4x when reprompts > 1 (be conservative for procurement).

Laura — I drafted a one-page procurement summary (short bullets + worst-case row) you can paste into the SOW appendix. I recommend we call out a "contract floor": commit to a pilot monthly spend cap and true-up after pilot.

If Sara's logs show higher repeat queries, numbers improve; if they show more cold sessions, prepare for the worst-case lane.

Ben
Senior FinOps Analyst | Redwood Inference
attachments: prefetch-sim-results.csv (text/csv)

Sara —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. We've attached a concise procurement-ready summary and a sensitivity table based on Ben's simulations. Key callouts for your PO team:
- Worst-case tokens/$ (use for budgeting): 950 tokens/$.
- Recommended contractual structure: pilot month billed on invoice tied to milestone (pilot activation), then monthly steady billing with a 30-day true-up.
- SOW appendix: includes default batching/prefetch settings with an explicit clause to retune settings after pilot (no change fees for tuning during the first 60 days).

Attachments: token_model_v2.xlsx (detailed workbook), MAP_action_items.pdf (action list), prefetch-sim-results.csv

Next steps: Beacon provides sample logs (Sara said by 6/15) -> we run prefetch sim -> finalize numbers by EOD 6/24 -> procurement issues PO -> target signature 6/30. If procurement needs a slightly larger buffer, we can provide a two-week extension on the PO window.

Let me know if procurement wants the worst-case row highlighted in the SOW or a separate one-page appendix.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
